contains.zcull_poll_no_wait_616: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_POLL_NO_WAIT_616 (VKGSRender.cpp check_occlusion_query_status): a non-forced ZCULL poll reports a query ready only when gathering its host queries (one per command buffer it spans, oldest first until the first hit, all of them in precise mode) will not wait for the GPU; upstream checks only the oldest one, so a poll whose oldest part found no hit waited in MoltenVK for the command buffer a zcull_sync hint had just submitted. contains.zclip_window_z_616: REWINDBOX_ZCLIP_WINDOW_Z_616 (RSXVertexPrologue.glsl, GLSLTypes.h, GLSLCommon.cpp, VKVertexProgram.cpp, title lever): Black Ops II (BLES01717) only. Without float64 nor an unrestricted depth range (MoltenVK) the vertex fallback compresses Z above 1 into [0.99, 1] from window Z (d) instead of clip-space Z (pos.z). The BLES01717 capture of RPCS3 issue #13227 draws 26 of 4,023 draws with clip [1, 1e19], viewport Z scale 1e19 over offset 1, reversed depth GEQUAL (12-draw depth prepass, 12-draw colour pass, 2 blended); the upstream fallback gives every fragment of those draws depth 1.0 (host test), so the colour pass keeps the last triangle drawn instead of the nearest; with window Z the depth follows the view distance (1.0 to 0.9901). The SPIR-V of every other title is byte-identical (glslang); Black Ops II vertex Metal libraries are compiled again once
contains.spu_object_prefetch_616: REWINDBOX_SPU_OBJECT_PREFETCH_616 (ios/IOSSpuObjectPrefetch.h, JITLLVM.cpp, SPUCommonRecompiler.cpp, System.cpp, title lever): Black Ops II (BLES01717) only. After the SPU object-cache eviction plan, one utility-class thread reads the title's compressed objects into memory (newest first, 48 MiB budget, objects up to 256 KiB); a compile thread takes an object's bytes once and inflates and validates them as after its own read; an object not read yet is claimed and read from disk as before, never awaited; the store is emptied when emulation stops. Build 614 logs: 7,162 object reads (4,300.8 ms, 0.6 ms each) in the first window of a multiplayer match with the 2,038.7 ms frame 2388, and a 613-read burst with the 1,121.4 ms frame 3537, both without a blocking pipeline. JITCacheCompatibility.cmake maps the exact JITLLVM.cpp and SPUCommonRecompiler.cpp to their delivered Core 613 effective hashes
contains.core616_20261102: the Core 616 record (Core 613 record, ZCULL poll without wait and its probe for every title; Black Ops II pinned-depth window Z and SPU object read-ahead), unchanged in behaviour; build-utils/rpcs3/core619-from-616.patch (insertions only) turns its files into the Core 619 files
contains.zcull_on_demand_619: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_ON_DEMAND_619 (ios/IOSZcullOnDemand.h, ios/IOSRsxLabelAccess.h, RSXZCULL.cpp/.h, RSXThread.h, nv47_sync.hpp, nv406e.cpp, nv4097.cpp, rsx_methods.cpp, cellGcmSys.cpp, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp, title lever): Assassin's Creed (BLES00158, BLUS30089) only. Upstream marks a report location 'accessed' for the rest of the boot after the first access to a page that still holds a pending report; every report is then critical and every label write with a pipe flush, WAIT_FOR_IDLE or NOTIFY waits for the GPU in ZCULL_control::sync(). Build 617 logs (PID 65755, session 1, windows 17-28): 2,203-2,911 such waits per 5 s window, 4.15-4.32 s in all, every other ZCULL read path at 0, 14-17 FPS. On iOS the host page is 16 KiB: the GCM labels (4 KiB), the notifies (1 KiB) and local reports 0-703 share one page (label area 0x40300000 in the Black Ops II logs), so the RSX thread's own label read in write_gcm_label is enough to trigger it (independent review). With the lever, report pages stay protected; the RSX thread reaches the GCM label/report area and locked report pages through the unprotected view (label writes and reads, semaphore acquire, notify, flip label, conditional render and forwarder reads); a PPU or SPU access to a page with a pending report asks the RSX thread (pipe_flush_interrupt) to write every claimed report as sync() does, waits for it, then unprotects the page; an RSX copy out of a locked page writes them first; the HLE timestamp reads go through the protected view. The guest reads the same values, the labels no longer wait. A request not picked up in 2 s, not completed in 5 s, guest waits above 400 ms per second, more than 1,000 services per second, any other faulting thread, a stopping emulator or Accurate RSX reservation access keep or return the boot to the upstream mode; sync() and update() reached inside a pass return at once. COREPROF ZCULLDEMAND619 counts faults by label/report/other offset, services, waits, timeouts, the trip reason and, for every title, which access switched a location to the upstream mode
contains.zclip_pinned_affine_619: REWINDBOX_ZCLIP_PINNED_AFFINE_619 (RSXVertexPrologue.glsl, GLSLTypes.h, GLSLCommon.cpp, VKVertexProgram.cpp, title lever): Black Ops II (BLES01717) only, on top of REWINDBOX_ZCLIP_WINDOW_Z_616. The fallback compressed only window Z in (1, far] and passed every other vertex through; the pinned draws of the #13227 capture keep depth clip on and clamp off (NV4097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL = 1), so a triangle with a vertex in front of the near plane (window Z above 1e19) mixed an unchanged vertex with compressed ones and Vulkan clipped its edges at about 1e-21 of their length (host test) instead of at the near plane: the part of the first-person arm crossing the near plane vanished (Build 617 report: no texture on the back of the arm). For a clip range wholly above 1 every vertex now takes the same affine map of [near, far] onto [0.99, 1], unclamped beyond far: the hardware clip point equals the RSX clip point (host test, 5 edges) and every vertex in (1, far] keeps its Core 616 value. The SPIR-V of every other shader is byte-identical (glslang); Black Ops II vertex Metal libraries are compiled again once

contains.gpu_timing_621: REWINDBOX_GPU_TIMING_621 (ios/IOSGpuTiming.h, VKGSRender.cpp/.h, VKGSRenderTypes.hpp, VKPresent.cpp, VKCommandStream.cpp, vkutils/device.cpp/.h, RSXThread.cpp, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp, system_config.h, RPCS3IOSExperimentalPolicy.*, RPCS3IOSBootDiagnostics.h, System.cpp): every title. The reference traces print gpu_execution_ms=-1. In MoltenVK 1.4.2 (db66022) the MTLCommandBuffer GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime are read nowhere and VK_EXT_metal_objects does not export command buffers; vkGetPerformanceStatisticsMVK is a CPU commit-to-completion interval; Vulkan timestamp queries are sampled on Apple GPUs at Metal stage boundaries (a one-byte blit pass per timestamp, deferred to the end of the encoder batch, waiting for the previous encoders) and resolved from an MTLCounterSampleBuffer after completion. Each VKGSRender primary chunk (512) records a TOP_OF_PIPE timestamp when its recording begins and a BOTTOM_OF_PIPE one before vkEndCommandBuffer; the results are read without the WAIT bit when the chunk's fence signalled (frame-end sweep, at most 64) or before the chunk is reused (after the renderer's own wait), attributed to the renderer session and to the RSX frame whose on_frame_end closes the submission's epoch; overlapping submissions are united (never counted twice); VK_EXT_calibrated_timestamps pairs measure the GPU tick rate against the host clock (MoltenVK reports timestampPeriod 1.0) and place the GPU start on the host clock (queue delay, domain violations). COREPROF GPUTIME621 per window (coverage, busy, overlap, pending, unavailable, late and stop drops, units, probe CPU cost, blit passes); COREPROF FRAMECAUSE_EVENT gains gpu_execution_ms (or -1 with gpu_status), the waits and cause= with certainty=; GPU Timing Probe setting (Automatic = on) to measure its cost
contains.freeze_episode_621: REWINDBOX_FREEZE_EPISODE_621 (RPCS3IOSFreezeEpisode.h, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp, RPCS3IOSFreezeDump.cpp/.h, RPCS3IOSProfilerHelpers.h): the 5 s window trigger (running, no frame for 3 s, one group above half a core, one dump per 30 s) becomes episodes evaluated every 500 ms on a running-time clock that stops while paused, loading, stopping or suspended (no sample for 2 s); a busy stall begins at 3 s, a quiet one (below half a core) at 6 s, a guest-fault freeze (frozen state) at once; one FREEZE_DUMP per episode with a waits summary (PPU calls, SPU calls, SPU group states) and its episode id, the frozen state dumped too, 10 s floor; FREEZE_EPISODE begin/update/end lines (paused, suspended and loading time, flips during the episode, busiest threads, the RSX semaphore watch); recovery needs 10 flips over 1 s of running time, a later stall is a new episode
contains.iso_image_lifetime_621: REWINDBOX_ISO_IMAGE_LIFETIME_621 (Loader/ISO.cpp/.h, ISO.h newly carried): every file opened on the mounted disc re-opened DiscImages/<ID>/disc.iso by path; renamed or deleted during the session, the open still succeeded and the first read threw "Null object." on the PPU thread (host test with the real ISO.cpp). iso_archive keeps the image opened once when it parses it and every iso_file reads it through pread (own position), so the image lives until the device and its last open file are gone; a file that cannot be opened is refused (noent) instead; raw optical devices keep their per-file path
contains.zcull_621: REWINDBOX_ZCULL_FRAME_621, REWINDBOX_ZCULL_DEMAND_GUARD_621, REWINDBOX_ZCULL_DEMAND_BO2_621 (ios/IOSZcullOnDemand.h, RSXZCULL.cpp/.h, VKQueryPool.cpp, IOSFrameTrace.h, IOSGpuTiming.h, IOSTitleLevers.h, system_config.h, RPCS3IOSExperimentalPolicy.cpp, RPCS3IOSSettings.cpp, RPCS3IOSBootDiagnostics.h, System.cpp, RPCS3IOSPerformance.cpp), from the Build 620 iPhone logs (2 November 2026, PIDs 66891/66907/66957, Core 619): Assassin's Creed tripped the 619 on-demand lever in its first gameplay second (54 reads, 401.5 ms against a 400 ms one-second budget) and ran the rest of the boot in the upstream mode: 2,100-2,900 GPU syncs, 3.4-4.3 s of the RSX thread blocked per 5 s window, 14-18 FPS; Black Ops II took the upstream switch at every boot and waited 1.1-1.9 s per 5 s multiplayer window (200-390 syncs). The lever now trips on sustained guest waits only (one thread above 400 ms in 3 consecutive seconds, or above 900 ms over 16 waits in one second; all threads above 800 ms in 3 consecutive seconds), logs the trip as COREPROF ZCULLTRIP621 and splits each wait into pickup and service; Black Ops II joins the title list; the ZCULL On-Demand Reads setting tests the other mode per game; FRAMECAUSE_EVENT reports zcull_wait_ms per frame and cause=zcull_sync (cause_rule=v2)
